grh_71f4ffbed15710a89852.title: It Had to Be You
paragraphs: Wealthy young sculptor Vicki Stafford is preparing to marry the respectable Oliver Harrington when a dashing man named George suddenly steps out of her imagination and begins disrupting the match. George insists that he is only a figment created from Vickiâ€™s dreams and that his purpose is to keep her from marrying the wrong man. As Vicki falls in love with him, childhood photographs reveal the real source of the fantasy: George looks exactly like Johnny Blaine, the little boy Vicki adored years earlier. George understands that Vicki is not meant for a dream at all but for the real Johnny, and arranges one last interruption of the wedding by calling the fire department. Fireman Johnny Blaine arrives, Vicki recognizes him instantly, and George disappears with his mission complete as the two childhood sweethearts rediscover each other.

grh_713a6c1cfa27281b13d0.title: Leavin' Cheyenne
paragraphs: As the era of the great cattle drives fades, older trail cook Samuel and young wrangler Ross find themselves out of work and camping outside Cheyenne. Ross is nursing a head injury from a saloon fight caused by a woman and a confidence trick, while Samuel tries to teach him that pride, honor and gunplay mean something different off the trail than they did in the old cattle outfits. Their argument exposes the widening gap between Ross's romantic image of the West and Samuel's hard-earned realism. When Samuel decides to return to town for a battered frying pan that has been his companion for nineteen years, Ross insists on going with him because Samuel is his friend. Their uneasy loyalty becomes the thing that survives as the old trail life disappears.

grh_7142ddbae627feab93c1.title: Guess Who's Coming to California
paragraphs: Greg and Lois Edwards hope for a quiet California summer while their children are away, but their old friends Harry and Thelma Newman arrive as self-invited house guests. The Newmans fill every day with tourist plans, gambling, cemetery visits, dubious real-estate schemes and constant commotion, leaving Greg and Lois desperate for peace without wanting to hurt their friends. Greg reluctantly agrees to accompany Harry on a sales trip for desert property, but before they can go a small earthquake shakes the house. Terrified, Harry and Thelma immediately flee California for home. Greg and Lois finally celebrate having the house to themselves, only to receive a call announcing that Lois's mother is arriving the next day.

grh_715e4d7dfcbfb358f117.title: Cheyenne Express
paragraphs: Former gang member Wilbur English has shot outlaw Floyd Winters in the back and now lives in terror that Floyd's brother Russ will kill him in revenge. Britt escorts the increasingly panicked English to Single Pine, where he ignores advice to wait for the sheriff and boards the Cheyenne Express to escape. Unknown to him, the sheriff's posse is chasing Russ, who boards the same train farther down the line. The moment English sees him he runs through the cars and plunges from the rear platform to his death, even though witnesses say Russ never made a move toward him.
